input.question: Why doesn't Disney just buy back the rights?
input.ground_truth: Contracts. 20th Century Fox currently has distribution deal for Fantastic Four films, so trying to break that deal might have some negative consequences that Disney might not want to bother with. Also, it's worth pointing out that as far as Marvel's roster of superheroes go, the Fantastic Four are pretty craptastic. The money makers for Marvel have always been heroes like Spider-Man, the Hulk, Iron Man, and Captain America. This is why we're seeing Disney so focused on the Avengers and the heroes that make up the team. Not many people are clamoring to see the Fantastic Four in action (especially after those first two movies), so Disney probably doesn't care enough to make an offer to buy the rights back. Now, if we were talking about someone like Spider-Man, Disney would probably shell out the cash. I just have a hard time imagining that the Fantastic Four is high up on the company's priority list.

Question: Why doesn't Disney just buy back the rights?

Okay! Imagine you have a really cool toy that you let your friend borrow for a long time. But now, your friend owns the toy because they took care of it for so long and made it even more special. If you want the toy back, you can’t just take it—you have to ask your friend and maybe give them something nice in return, or agree on a new deal.

That’s kind of like what happens with Disney and the rights to some stories or movies. Disney didn’t always own them, and now someone else does because they bought them or made them really popular. If Disney wants them back, they have to ask nicely and maybe give something or make a good deal, instead of just taking them back.
